To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pre-otic region, which does not form somitic tissue but is the source for head muscle precursors, expresses the somitic transcription factors Lbx1, Paraxis and Pax7.

the lateral rectus is the only head muscle that develops according to the somitic program and that the pre-otic mesoderm and the lateral rectus precursor domain are defined by a distinct set of markers.

the pre-otic mesoderm, which forms the lateral rectus precursor, is distinct from the trunk somitic mesoderm in the regulation and function of the myogenic transcription factors Lbx1, Paraxis and Pax7, and that this difference reflects the distinct function and evolution of the lateral rectuses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the formation of the lateral rect muscle and the role that the lateral rect muscle plays during the development of the eye.
the mechanisms that control the development and differentiation of skeletal muscle in vertebrates.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the specification and differentiation of muscle precursors during vertebrate development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the head mesoderm has a unique identity and a unique set of regulatory cascades, and this identity is maintained even when the cells are transplanted into the trunk.
head and trunk myoblasts have a different origin, and that the regulatory cascades for the development of head myoblasts are different from those for trunk myoblast development.
the pre-otic mesoderm is the source of lateral rectus precursers, and that these cells are non-migrating and non-somite derived.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the head and trunk muscles develop by distinct regulatory cascades.
the pre-otic region of the head mesoderm is a unique domain of mesodermal development, with its own set of regulatory cascades and developmental programs.
the lateral rectus muscles are derived from pre-otic head paraxial mesoderm and that they are specified by a distinct set of markers that differ from the trunk myogenic markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
head muscles arise from a mesodermal domain distinct from somites.
Lbx1, Paraxis and Pax7 are expressed in the head in a regionalised and non-overlapping manner, and that the expression of these markers in the head is independent of the somitic regulatory cascade.
Lbx1 and Paraxis play distinct roles in the development of the lateral rectu and trunk muscles.
